subject: Urgent: FastFin production 5xx/latency spike on /generate (reserved capacity)
messages:
From: Sally Lewis <sally.lewis@fastfin.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastfin.com, Ahmed Patel <ahmed.patel@fastfin.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Timeouts & 500s on /generate - FastFin prod (reserved capacity)

Irene —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors and timeouts on our /generate endpoint at ~08:25 PDT. Errors are primarily 502/504 and elevated P95 latency (6–10s). We are on reserved capacity with you under FF-2019-42 and this is impacting customer transactions now (payments flow).

Attached: a short sample of application-side errors (fastfin_error_sample.log).

What we see:
- Rapid queue growth on requests to model: rdw-7b-instruct (our pinned model).
- Requests often include 4k token contexts (debugging shows repeated large prefixes).

Can you triage immediately? We need ETA on mitigation and whether autoscale or bursting is possible (we were told reserved is isolated). Please escalate.

—Sally
FastFin Production Ops
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sally Lewis <sally.lewis@fastfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeouts & 500s on /generate - FastFin prod (reserved capacity)

Sally —

Thanks for the alert and the log sample. I've looped in Marissa (ops) and David (CS/contract). We're triaging now. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the 4k contexts are a new change or a recurring pattern? Also, are you seeing a sudden increase in QPS or are these longer-running requests causing headroom exhaustion?

Immediate mitigation we will attempt:
1) Short-term throttling: gate long-context requests from the most aggressive client apps (we can enact a tenant-level rate limit within ~10–20m).
2) Model fallback: enable a smaller rdw-3b-quant variant for non-critical requests to relieve the reserved pool.
3) Ops runbook: Marissa will collect GPU pool metrics and check KV cache behavior.

If reserved headroom is truly saturated we'll need exec sign-off for emergency burst into nearby spare Dedicated capacity (this incurs usage beyond the reserved commit). Marissa, please share a quick cost estimate and pool id.

I will keep you posted every 15–30 minutes until resolved.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeouts & 500s on /generate - FastFin prod (reserved capacity)

Team — quick triage notes (pulling metrics and screenshots attached: pool_metrics_20260719.png):

What we observed:
- Reserved pool RDP-az2-pool-7 is at 98–100% GPU utilization across the last 8 min.
- Queue length (per-worker) jumped from median 6 -> 42 in a 6-minute window.
- P95 token generation time increased due to repeated KV cache misses — looks like long shared prefixes (4k contexts) are thrashing per-tenant KV cache and causing eviction churn.
- No node failures, but throughput dropped as scheduler spends cycles on cache management and small-batch inefficiencies.

Suggested immediate actions (minutes to an hour):
A) Tenant gate: apply temporary rate cap on requests with context length > 2000 tokens at edge (reduces churn).
B) Enable per-tenant prefix caching (config flip) for FastFin — reduces repeated prefix re-computation (expected ~25–40% token cost reduction for their traffic pattern).
C) Promote non-critical traffic to rdw-3b-quant fallback route for up to 30% of requests (low-latency but lower quality).
D) If A–C insufficient, approve emergency burst into dedicated spare capacity (we have a nearby spare capacity pool with capacity for ~60% of current demand) for a 6–12 hour window while we tune autoscaling. Estimated incremental cost: $18k–$28k (ballpark for 12h at on-demand burst rates).

I can apply A and B immediately and monitor. If we move to D we need exec approval (billing sign-off + ops ticket to provision burst).

Attachments: pool_metrics_20260719.png, runbook_short.pdf (short checklist for throttling + fallback).

-M
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeouts & 500s on /generate - FastFin prod (reserved capacity)

Irene / Marissa —

From a CS / commercial perspective: FastFin is a priority account (FF-2019-42). Per the reserved contract we committed a baseline throughput; we need to be careful about unilateral throttles that could violate the contract. However, given immediate customer impact I support temporary protective measures if we accompany them with a clear remediation plan and customer communication.

Two asks for the exec path:
1) Authorize emergency burst spending up to $30k for immediate capacity relief (one-time, 12h). I'll draft the customer-facing note and the credit offer outline (pro-rata credit for any SLA breach).
2) Approve a temporary protective throttle on long-context requests (<= 2 hours CC to legal if needed) while Marissa tunes caching and autoscale.

If Vivek can greenlight the spend and the external communication language, I will coordinate the credit calculation and an explicit timeline for rollback.

-David
David Kim
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
david@redwood.com
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request: emergency burst + customer communication (FastFin)

Vivek —

We need an exec decision within the next 2 hours to avoid sustained customer-impact and potential churn. Summary and asks below.

Summary of impact:
- FastFin (FF-2019-42) experiencing P95 latency spike (6–10s), increased 5xx rate, payment flow degradation.
- Root cause signal: reserved pool RDP-az2-pool-7 near-saturation driven by high-context requests causing KV cache thrash.
- Immediate mitigation available: tenant rate cap + prefix caching + route partial traffic to rdw-3b-quant. These reduce load but may not fully restore throughput in peak windows.

Asks (decision + nominal approval):
1) Approve emergency burst into spare Dedicated capacity for up to 12 hours. Cost cap requested: $30,000 one-time. Purpose: immediate traffic relief while we implement longer-term fixes.
2) Approve customer credit framework: pro-rata credit for SLA deviation (preliminary suggested credit: 10% of July invoice for impacted endpoints; David will finalize).
3) Approve outbound customer note (I will send) that describes actions taken, expected timeline, and credit offer.

Risk / mitigation notes:
- If we do not approve burst, we will continue with A/B/C (rate cap + prefix caching + fallback) and expect partial restoration within 30–90 minutes but risk repeated degradation during peak spikes.
- Emergency burst will stabilize customer traffic quickly but increases variable cost and sets a precedent; recommend follow-up: dedicated headroom re-evaluation and configuration changes (permanent prefix caching for high-context tenants, revised commit for FastFin).

Requested decision window: respond by 12:47 PDT to avoid storm at peak traffic at ~13:00–14:00 PDT.

I will coordinate execution immediately upon approval.

Thanks,
Irene
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 11:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec approval request: emergency burst + customer communication (FastFin)

Irene / team —

Approved: emergency burst up to $30k and greenlight for outbound customer note. Please proceed with A/B/C immediately and provision burst in parallel.

Conditions:
- Marissa: document the exact start/end times and pool id for billing reconciliation.
- David: finalize the credit computation and include a short-term remediation commit (timeline to eliminate repeated KV thrash).
- Irene: send the customer note; keep language factual and apologize for impact.

Thanks for the rapid triage. Keep updates flowing in this thread.

-Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
